name: Poly Network exploiter
about: The address behind the 2021 Poly Network hack, about $610M taken and later returned

labels.name: The shared multisig (Poly and the hacker)
The address he wrote to as "Dear Poly"

beats.title: The first coins
beats.text: 9 August 2021. A small 0.47 ETH arrives at a fresh address: enough to pay for what comes next.

beats.title: The trick
beats.text: 10 August. A single call to Poly Network's cross-chain manager makes it believe this address may move the bridge's funds.

beats.title: The vault empties
beats.text: In 36 minutes Poly's vault pays out ten times: $96.4M in USDC, $82M in WETH, $47.5M in WBTC, $33.4M in USDT, $9M in ETH, and some SHIB, UNI, DAI, renBTC and FEI. About $273.6M on Ethereum alone.

beats.title: A tip of 13.37 ETH
beats.text: He sends 13.37 ETH to a stranger. Later he explains: "I feeled the warmth from the Ethereum community."

beats.title: Away from the coins that can be frozen
beats.text: USDC and USDT can be frozen by the companies behind them. He puts the $96.4M of USDC into Curve's pool and takes out $96.9M of DAI, which nobody can freeze. The USDT is frozen and never moves again. "How about unlocking my USDT after returning enough USDC?"

beats.title: He starts talking
beats.text: Messages written into his own transactions: "Wonder why Tornado? Will miner stop me?" Forty minutes later: "It would have been a billion hack… now considering returning some tokens." Strangers write back by the hundred.

beats.title: The turn
beats.text: 11 August. "Ready to return the fund! … I need a secured multisig wallet from you."

beats.title: The first returns
beats.text: FEI, SHIB, renBTC and UNI, about $4.6M, go back to Poly's multisig. In between, his Q&A, parts one to four: "Why hacking? For fun :)"

beats.title: The big return
beats.text: 12 August. "Just confirmed the shared multisig wallet with the Poly!!!" Within two hours $46.1M in WBTC, $95.4M in DAI and 28,953 ETH ($88.3M) go to a multisig he shares with Poly. He publishes Poly's $500k bounty offer and says he will send everything back instead.

beats.title: The diary
beats.text: For ten more days he writes: Q&A parts five to eight, lessons for "DeFi noobs", notes to the press. His USDT stays frozen; he keeps asking Poly to have it unlocked.

beats.title: The end
beats.text: 23 August. "Dear Poly team, keep calm and this is the happy ending!"

beats.title: An empty castle
beats.text: About $3,500 is left, and four years of junk tokens and NFTs that strangers keep sending. On Ethereum about $273.6M came in and about $234.5M went back. The $33.4M of USDT that Tether froze is no longer in the wallet either: the address is still on Tether's blacklist and holds $6.99 of USDT today, though it never sent the USDT anywhere. 13.37 ETH went to a stranger.
